diagnosis: The paired sample does not show a global Base score regression, but its small partial-score gain costs 6.36 times the elapsed time and 5.93 times the model interactions.

The main amplification is orchestration: mandatory generic development and test reports are published, searched, read, and selected even though participant messages and Host Tool facts already carry the current execution result.
Independent verification finds real omissions, but six cases enter repeated Developer and Tester phases; internal PASS does not reliably predict the official strict score.

The runtime adherence checker incorrectly required mounted agents with no benchmark-client call to load the Skill. Actual client callers still need to load the named Skill before their first call, including calls through interpreter flags or absolute script paths.
Tester is not broadly corrupting state: it made four business mutations across 13 cases. The dominant defect is expensive discovery and repair coordination with weak stopping criteria.
limitations: No intermediate WorldState snapshots were retained at every role boundary, so exact Developer-only and post-repair official scores cannot be reconstructed without changing evidence.
Prompt and checker corrections are zero-model verified. Their live score and redundant-call reduction remain unmeasured until a newly authorized controlled run.
